[WP]You are the world's greatest healer - you can bring anyone back from the brink of death, and sometimes even beyond. But something happened, something big - and you swore never heal anyone again.

He stared with empty eyes into the rain beyond the door. Why is it, he wondered, that the rain always brought death to his door?

A flash of lightning illuminated, for a brief moment, the lone rider heading through the valley. His horse threatened to fall beneath him as his remorseless spurs dug deep into its sides. With a scream of pain, the horse stumbled - and all was dark once more.

Thunder echoed throughout the valley.

He poured another cup of tea - and carefully reset the board before him. That lightning-flash had told him all he needed to know. He could even picture the battle within his head, as clearly as though he had been at the scene himself.

A poisoned arrow, embedded into the left forearm. A numbing, crawling poison that threatened to creep into the heart, closer, closer, inches away - then, an amputation. Good thinking - probably saved his life - but poor technique, compounded by the awkward position and awkward tools.

Profuse bleeding, held back only by crudest of wrappings. Unconciousness should have taken place hours ago - the fact that he was still alive, much less riding through the rain, was testament to his great constitution. Truly, this was an exceptional swordsman. Quick-thinking, to save his life with the sacrifice of his arm. Great strength, of both arm and character, to lope off his own arm. And finally - of great willpower and body, to have survived the ordeal, much less gotten on a horse less than 3 hours later.

Which left only one question to be answered - if he was so skilled, who could have done this to him?

A clash of thunder interrupted his thoughts. Blood had begun to trickle in through the cracks of the door.

He made no move to open the door. Instead, he began to sip daintily from the teacup, pondering the intricate puzzle of the Igo board that he had arranged.

A bloody fist hammered on the door. "Doctor." It rasped. "Doctor!"

He took another sip from the tea. Two hours until he bled out. At most two and a half, given his extraordinary aptitude for survival thus far.

"Doctor." Called the disembodied voice, "Doctor."

Hesitantly, he placed the white piece onto the edge of the board. Fifty-four moves to the domination of the centre; thirty-seven moves to the enemy's Eye. It was a good move. And yet...

"Doctor, I know you won't help me. I know your reputation by now; everyone does!" The voice laughed, the frenzied laughter of a hunted man, a dying man.

Ah; black's perfect counter. He frowned, brows furrowed deep in thought. Yes; in that case, it would only take thirty two moves to complete the encirclement for the blacks. A carefully laid-out trap. He took another sip of the tea.

"But please - I have a message that you must hear." The voice fell into a faint whisper barely audible over the patter of rain. "Please, doctor - it's no trick. It involves your life."

In which case, white had no choice but to take the original move. Tried, but true, He removed the first piece, and began to move it towards the centre, when...

"It involves The Seven Devil-Gods." A sigh, a slump; the sound of a corpse leaning, then sliding on the door.

The white piece remained frozen in midair.
